briefing.headline: Harbour and Kestrel draw 2-2

first_half.text: Kestrel were compact centrally but had less possession and fewer final-third entries in the first half.

changes.text: Kestrel pushed more through the centre and increased centre-channel entries, while Harbour pulled their attacking focus away from the centre.
Harbour's pressing and high regain rate dropped notably after the break, with lower turnover height and fewer high regains.

predictions.text: Harbour did not shift right; right-channel entries fell rather than rising.
Harbour's PPDA rose only marginally (6%), well short of the predicted 20% increase.
Kestrel's centre entries increased rather than being cut, so Harbour failed to reduce the central overload.
Harbour's high regains fell by 50% after the break, consistent with Kestrel sitting deeper.
Kestrel increased their possession by 12 percentage points after the break, achieving the predicted rise.
Harbour's centre entries fell by 40% after the break as Kestrel crowded the middle.

result.text: Harbour's shot volume and xG dropped in the second half as their final-third entries and high regains declined, reducing their control of the contest.

removed_claims: first_half: Harbour dominated the final third and created the clearer chance volume to lead 2-0 at the break.
first_half: They pressed high and won the ball frequently in advanced areas, producing many high regains and very high turnover height.
changes: Kestrel shifted the territorial balance after half-time, increasing their overall and final-third possession while Harbour's possession fell.
result: Kestrel converted their second-half territorial advantage into chances and goals, overturning the momentum to salvage a 2-2 draw.
result: The tactical flip was clear: Kestrel pushed through the centre and secured more possession while Harbour withdrew from advanced pressing, and that shift produced the comeback.
headline: Kestrel overturn 2-0 halftime deficit to draw 2-2 as the momentum and territorial control flipped after the break (replaced by the template headline)
